answer: Each agent must reconcile a bonded cold-wallet reserve against a hot-wallet ledger, so a sybil cluster needs real capital locked per identity, turning a tide of fake accounts into a costly balance-sheet liability. Every identity carries a distinct pigment of transaction history the exchange auditor can trace, since shared funding wallets expose coordinated fakes. A walnut of doubt remains where attackers self-fund through many small deposits, yet full-reserve attestation still prices each sybil at locked collateral, capping the attack.
